It restricts Network Access Account information to supported OSD media task-sequence scenarios. An internal service required for device compliance checks will be deprecated in October 2026; Software Center compliance checks may fail in co-managed environments where the Compliance workload is managed by Intune, so Microsoft says to apply the update before October. The release also removes the deprecated SQL Server

keyChanges.title: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS support arrives before Ubuntu 22.04’s August deadline
keyChanges.detail: Intune now supports Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. Support for Ubuntu 22.04 LTS ends in August 2026, although devices already enrolled on 22.04 remain enrolled. Administrators can find them under Devices > All devices by filtering for Linux and adding the OS version column, then notify users to upgrade to a supported Ubuntu version.

keyChanges.title: Platform SSO registration is documented for macOS Automated Device Enrollment
keyChanges.detail: The Intune What's new entry documents running Platform SSO during macOS ADE registration. Before enrollment, administrators must configure the settings catalog setting Enable Registration During Setup, deploy Company Portal version 5.2604.0 or newer as a line-of-business app, and configure ADE to use Setup Assistant with modern authentication and await final configuration. The scenario applies to macOS 26 and newer and gives users access to Microsoft Entra ID resources immediately at the desktop.

keyChanges.title: Windows Security Center MAM setup now requires an explicit connector toggle
keyChanges.detail: The revised Edge data-security procedure says to open the Windows Security Center connector after creating it, turn on Connect Windows devices for MAM, and save. The documented status is Available after creation and changes to Enabled only after the toggle is turned on, replacing earlier guidance that the connector remained Unavailable until an App Protection Policy arrived or a MAM user enrolled. This is a procedure and status-documentation change, not a stated preview or GA announcement.

keyChanges.title: Unlicensed administrator defaults now depend on tenant creation date
keyChanges.detail: Tenants created after July 2021 support unlicensed administrator access by default and require no action. Tenants created before July 2021 require the Allow access to unlicensed admins setting, and Microsoft says the setting cannot be undone after activation. The guidance also clarifies the limit of 350 unlicensed administrators per security group, that multiple groups can be used above that limit, and that nested-group members are not included.

2026-05-04.headline: Controlled Configuration preview makes Defender antivirus policy authoritative over legacy settings
2026-05-04.overview: Intune’s period was maintenance-heavy: 239 entries were updated, no Message Center items appeared, and many representative edits changed links, headings, terminology, or requirements formatting rather than documented service behavior. The meaningful exceptions concern security and platform changes: Controlled Configuration is explicitly headed to public preview; Apple’s 26.4 guidance redirects deprecated Intelligence controls to DDM; Strict Tunnel Mode is in development for Android; and the MTD connector guidance defines a tightly scoped Android role.
2026-05-04.adminImpact: Treat Controlled Configuration and Strict Tunnel Mode as preview or roadmap planning material, not general-availability announcements. For design reviews, account for Controlled Configuration’s precedence over Group Policy, Configuration Manager, and local changes; verify Android Management API and Always On VPN dependencies for Tunnel; and map Apple Intelligence controls to DDM for version 26.4 and later. Audit custom-compliance scripts against the 2,048-character output limit and error 65009 risk. The MTD role has a one-partner-per-tenant constraint and excludes personally owned work profiles; ordinary link and heading edits do not call for tenant changes.

keyChanges.title: Controlled Configuration enters public preview for Defender antivirus
keyChanges.detail: The In Development guidance explicitly says Intune is bringing Controlled Configuration (CC) to public preview for Microsoft Defender antivirus settings. When enabled, settings delivered by Intune or Microsoft Defender for Endpoint security settings management override Group Policy, Configuration Manager, local changes, and scripts. CC also extends Tamper Protection by allowing administrators to lock settings to defined values rather than only defaults. This is a policy-precedence change to plan for, not a general-

keyChanges.title: Apple Intelligence controls shift from deprecated MDM restrictions to DDM
keyChanges.detail: For iOS/iPadOS and macOS devices running version 26.4 and later, the guidance says Apple deprecated Intelligence-related settings in the MDM restrictions payload. It directs administrators to the DDM configurations released in March 2026. The deprecated list includes controls for Assistant, Dictation, Genmoji, Writing Tools, Siri, predictive keyboards, spell check, and related features. This is a platform-driven migration path, not a new Intune setting launch.

keyChanges.title: Strict Tunnel Mode is planned for Android Microsoft Tunnel
keyChanges.detail: The roadmap says Microsoft Tunnel will add Strict Tunnel Mode for Android Enterprise devices enrolled through Android Management API, configured with Always On VPN. It will force traffic through the tunnel and block traffic if the connection drops, while an app exclusion list allows specified apps to bypass the tunnel. The guidance also describes support for unenrolled devices using Microsoft Tunnel for Mobile Application Management. The capability remains in development.

keyChanges.title: MTD connector guidance adds Android role permissions with a one-partner limit
keyChanges.detail: The connector documentation adds a fourth category, Mobile Threat Defense role, with a toggle that grants the selected partner exemptions from app suspension, hibernation, power restrictions, and user controls on Android Enterprise corporate-owned fully managed and corporate-owned work profile devices. Only one MTD partner can hold the role per tenant; the connector must be configured, its app targeted, and devices enrolled through Android Management API. Personally owned work profiles are not supported. The change

keyChanges.title: Custom-compliance discovery output has a 2,048-character ceiling
keyChanges.detail: An added warning in Create Policy says discovery-script output is limited to 2,048 characters. Output beyond that may be truncated, producing invalid JSON and error 65009 during compliance evaluation. Administrators should keep output concise or split large rule sets across multiple policies. This is operational guidance about custom compliance, not a launch or support change.

2026-05-11.headline: Windows Autopilot automatic mode for Windows 365 drops preview label in updated guidance
2026-05-11.overview: The week was mostly documentation maintenance: 129 of 132 changes were updates involving terminology, links, numbering, formatting, and procedure clarification. The notable administrator-facing exceptions were Windows Autopilot device preparation for Windows 365, the Security Copilot Vulnerability Remediation Agent permission model, and Intune’s Defender for Endpoint and Mobile Threat Defense setup guidance. The Autopilot articles remove “preview” and replace Windows 365 Frontline references with Windows 365 Flex. A new device-based Conditional Access how-to also makes its licensing, role, and compliance-policy prerequisites explicit. One standalone app-based Conditional Access how-to was removed, which the supplied evidence supports as documentation consolidation rather than retirement of the capability.
2026-05-11.adminImpact: Treat the Autopilot edit as a documentation and availability signal, not proof of general availability; confirm current Windows 365 and Autopilot availability before changing rollout plans. For the Vulnerability Remediation Agent, review the agentic user and delegated permissions assigned in Microsoft Entra and Microsoft Defender; the guidance lists Intune Read Only Operator or a custom role with Mobile apps/read and Device configurations/read. The agent remains documented as limited public preview and public-cloud only. If enabling the Defender for Endpoint automatic-launch toggle, also enable Grant MTD role permissions for Android Enterprise COBO and COPE devices. For device-based Conditional Access, confirm a Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 license, Security Administrator or Conditional‌ ‍‍

keyChanges.title: Windows 365 automatic-mode guidance drops the public-preview label
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Autopilot device-preparation automatic-mode article removes “(preview)” from its title, description, headings, and public-preview note. It also replaces Windows 365 Frontline shared and dedicated references with Windows 365 Flex. This is a documentation status and terminology change; it does not establish general availability on its own.

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability Remediation Agent guidance defines an agentic-user RBAC model
keyChanges.detail: Security Copilot guidance now describes an agentic-user permission model for running the Vulnerability Remediation Agent. Permissions are delegated outside the Intune admin center in Microsoft Entra and Microsoft Defender. On the Intune side, the guidance names Read Only Operator or a custom role with Mobile apps/read and Device configurations/read; users viewing results need corresponding read access.

keyChanges.title: Defender connector guidance documents automatic launch on Android COBO and COPE
keyChanges.detail: The Mobile Threat Defense connector guidance documents an “Automatically launch Microsoft Defender for Endpoint during setup” toggle for Android Enterprise corporate-owned fully managed and corporate-owned work profile devices. It is available only for the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint connector and requires the “Grant MTD role permissions” toggle to be enabled as well.
keyChanges.product: Intune Mobile Threat Defense connector / Defender for Endpoint

keyChanges.title: New device-based Conditional Access guide names setup prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: Intune added a dedicated how-to requiring a Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 license and either the Security administrator or Conditional Access administrator role. The procedure also requires Intune device compliance policies to be configured before creating the Conditional Access policy. This is a new documentation path, not evidence of a newly introduced Conditional Access capability.
keyChanges.product: Intune device compliance / Microsoft Entra Conditional Access

keyChanges.title: Custom compliance script uploads remain unable to use scope tags
keyChanges.detail: The revised custom-script guidance makes the limitation explicit: the upload workflow does not support scope tags. Administrators must have the default scope tag to create, edit, or view custom compliance discovery scripts.

2026-05-18.headline: EPM report access tightens as Intune flags device-reported compliance values as untrusted
2026-05-18.overview: The week was dominated by documentation maintenance—licensing-link moves, metadata changes, and template reshaping—but several updates carry concrete administrator consequences. EPM reporting guidance now describes an explicit permission requirement; Security Copilot guidance expands the documented default inheritance of Intune RBAC access; the Vulnerability Remediation Agent workflow and identity handling have changed; and new Cloud PKI guidance covers staged CA renewal. The supplied evidence contains no Message Center item and does not establish a new GA launch, retirement, or tenant-wide rollout.
2026-05-18.adminImpact: Audit custom EPM roles and Graph-based reporting access for the explicit View Reports permission. Review which Intune RBAC roles should inherit Security Copilot access when Intune is enabled as a data source. Update compliance-report procedures so device-reported values are treated as untrusted context, not an enforcement signal. For the Vulnerability Remediation Agent, verify delegated permissions and readiness-check procedures, and plan human-identity transitions before support expires. Cloud PKI administrators should review renewal permissions and staged-CA activation requirements before a CA expires.

keyChanges.title: EPM reports now require explicit View Reports permission
keyChanges.detail: The updated EPM reporting article states that access through the Intune admin center or Microsoft Graph requires Endpoint Privilege Management Policy Authoring > View Reports, also identified as EpmPolicy.ViewReports. Users without it receive HTTP 403 responses from the report endpoint. The article says Device configurations > Read previously provided access. Review custom roles and reporting clients that depend on the older permission.

keyChanges.title: Security Copilot guidance expands default Intune-role access inheritance
keyChanges.detail: When Microsoft Intune is enabled as a Security Copilot data source, the updated overview says the Microsoft Entra Intune Administrator role automatically inherits Security Copilot owner access, while all other built-in and custom Intune RBAC roles inherit Security Copilot contributor access. Existing Intune RBAC permissions and scope tags still limit accessible data and actions. Administrators can remove the default access by removing Intune roles from the Security Copilot contributor role.

keyChanges.title: Compliance guidance treats device-reported Setting values as untrusted input
keyChanges.detail: The Monitor Policy update explains that some compliance reports include a Setting column populated directly by a device, application, or administrator-supplied script, including custom compliance and Android app configuration scenarios. Intune does not validate or enforce the content; values can contain free-form text, URLs, file paths, or identifying and environment-specific information, and may attempt to influence administrator behavior. Use these values only as context, confirm status through trusted workflows,

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability Remediation Agent tightens identity setup and run readiness
keyChanges.detail: Updated Security Copilot instructions require administrators to delegate all required permissions to the agentic user and pass Run Readiness Check before runs are enabled; a successful check enables the Run button and scheduled runs. Agents using human identities must transition before support expires. Identity problems are handled by removing the agent and setting it up again rather than renewing or replacing the identity.

keyChanges.title: New Cloud PKI guidance documents staged CA renewal
keyChanges.detail: A new Cloud PKI article documents renewal for Intune-managed and bring-your-own-CA issuing CAs. Renewal always generates a new public/private key pair while preserving certificates and CRLs from earlier CA versions. A CA becomes eligible at half its validity lifetime or after expiry; an expired CA can be renewed, but certificate issuance remains unavailable until the staged CA is activated. The documented permissions are Read CAs and Create certificate authorities.

2026-05-25.headline: OpenClaw baseline reference warns Node.js and WSL controls may disrupt workloads
2026-05-25.overview: The week was mostly documentation maintenance, but several changes have direct planning value. The Intune security-baseline overview now lists Local AI Agent Baseline - OpenClaw as a Preview, while its new settings reference documents outbound Node.js/runtime controls and warns they may disrupt legitimate processes. Security Copilot’s Vulnerability Remediation Agent guidance changes from limited public preview for selected customers to public preview. New Intune licensing and account-move references clarify plan structure and regional data-at-rest moves; custom-compliance guidance now lists RedHat Enterprise Linux 10 rather than 8 and makes discovery-script sequencing explicit. Separately, iOS/iPadOS compliance references now say iOS 17.0 and later rather than iOS 8.0 and later for multiple settings. The removed Create App Based Policy page is a documentation retirement, not evidence that app-based Conditional Access was retired; much of the remaining work is terminology, link, and prerequisite-layout cleanup.
2026-05-25.adminImpact: Pilot and test the OpenClaw baseline, use the Properties catalog to inventory local AI agents, and review settings that could affect legitimate Node.js or Windows Subsystem for Linux workloads. Treat the Vulnerability Remediation Agent as public preview, not general availability. Use the new licensing and account-move references for entitlement and data-residency planning. Revalidate Linux and iOS compliance assumptions against the current references before changing policy guidance, because the supplied diffs alone do not establish a service-side enforcement change.

keyChanges.title: OpenClaw reference documents runtime controls and a deployment warning
keyChanges.detail: The new Intune settings reference says the baseline limits unauthorized local AI agents by disrupting common execution paths. It includes firewall rules that restrict outbound communication from runtime environments such as Node.js, plus controls that can affect Windows Subsystem for Linux and Node.js. The reference warns that the baseline may not block every execution path and may block other processes, so each setting should be reviewed and tested; it also points admins to Properties catalog inventory for Local ‌

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability Remediation Agent guidance changes from limited to public preview
keyChanges.detail: The setup article replaces wording that the feature was in limited public preview and available only to a select group of customers with a statement that it is in public preview, linking to Public preview in Microsoft Intune. This is a documented preview-status change, not a general-availability announcement or proof that every tenant has access.

keyChanges.title: New licensing reference maps Intune Plan 1, Plan 2, and Suite
keyChanges.detail: The new Microsoft Intune licensing article defines Plan 1 as the base service, Plan 2 as additive to Plan 1 with advanced capabilities including Remote Help and Advanced Analytics, and the Intune Suite as additive to Plan 1 and including Plan 2. It also states that users or devices benefiting directly or indirectly from Intune need an Intune license and documents a device-only subscription. This is a new reference and does not by itself show that entitlements changed.

keyChanges.title: Account-move guidance separates regional data moves from tenant migration
keyChanges.detail: The new overview says an Intune account move relocates customer data at rest between geographic datacenter regions while preserving the tenant, policies, profiles, device enrollments, app-management state, and service configuration. It explicitly says the process is not a tenant-to-tenant migration, and distinguishes customer-requested moves coordinated through Microsoft support from Microsoft-initiated moves with advance notice. This is planning guidance, not evidence that a move is scheduled for a tenant.

keyChanges.title: Custom-compliance guidance now lists RHEL 10 and script sequencing
keyChanges.detail: The custom-compliance guide changes its listed Linux distribution from RedHat Enterprise Linux 8 to RedHat Enterprise Linux 10. It also spells out that administrators must prepare a JSON file and discovery script, upload the script to the Microsoft Intune admin center before creating the policy, and use one script per compliance policy even though each script can discover multiple settings. This is a documentation update; the supplied diff does not prove that backend platform support changed.

2026-06-01.headline: CMG image deprecation drives Configuration Manager’s Windows Server 2022 transition
2026-06-01.overview: Configuration Manager’s CMG VMSS update is the week’s most consequential change: gateways are moving from the legacy Windows Server 2022 Azure Marketplace offer `windowsserver`, which includes .NET 6, to `windowsserver2022`. The legacy images will lose support and image-refresh OS updates, and new CMG deployments or reimaging will fail when enforcement begins in early 2027. Intune’s substantive changes were more focused: Local AI Agent/OpenClaw inventory guidance became more specific, Apple wired-network documentation now covers iOS/iPadOS as well as macOS, and the GCC High/DoD matrix distinguishes available Windows Autopilot device preparation from unsupported update capabilities. Most other edits were documentation maintenance; the dedicated Multi Admin Approval Graph API article was removed, while Remote Help references show differing version numbers rather than a new capability.
2026-06-01.adminImpact: Configuration Manager administrators should review CMG VMSS deployments and install KB37942646 through Updates and Servicing where applicable. It applies directly to versions 2603 and 2509, and to versions 2503 and 2409 with the required rollups; the 2509 second update rollup already includes it. CMG timing language changed during the week: an initial KB37784287 entry cited June 9, 2026, while later wording cites enforcement in early 2027, so validate the applicable current guidance before scheduling. Intune administrators collecting device properties should consider the recommended Host process field for OpenClaw discovery. Apple and government-cloud administrators should use the documented platform and cloud-specific scope, and audit automation runbooks that referenced the removed MAA–?

keyChanges.title: CMG VMSS update replaces legacy Windows Server 2022 images
keyChanges.detail: KB37942646 transitions the CMG virtual machine scale set from Azure Marketplace offer `windowsserver`, which includes .NET 6, to `windowsserver2022`, which does not. Legacy images will no longer be supported or receive new OS patch updates through image refresh; once enforcement begins in early 2027, new CMG deployments and reimaging operations that use them will fail. The update is available through Updates and Servicing for Configuration Manager 2603 and for 2503/2409 with the required rollups; 2509 includes itใน

keyChanges.title: Properties Catalog guidance sharpens Local AI Agent discovery
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Properties Catalog reference lists Agent Name, Install Location, Install Scope, and Host process for Local AI Agent inventory. Microsoft recommends collecting Host process because OpenClaw can run under process names such as `node.exe` or `wsl.exe`. The linked security baseline label also changed from “Local AI Agent Baseline - OpenClaw (Preview)” to “Local AI Agent Baseline - OpenClaw”; that terminology change alone does not establish general availability.

keyChanges.title: Apple wired-network reference expands documented scope to iOS/iPadOS
keyChanges.detail: The wired-network settings article changed from macOS-only wording to Apple devices and now explicitly covers iOS/iPadOS and macOS, with platform-specific sections and prerequisites. It states that the settings are available for all enrollment types and requires a wired network device configuration profile with the minimum Policy and Profile Manager role. The supplied diff establishes a documentation scope and prerequisite change, not a separate rollout announcement.

keyChanges.title: GCC High and DoD matrix marks Autopilot preparation available
keyChanges.detail: The government service table now marks Windows Autopilot device preparation as available and identifies user-driven deployments as available, while other device-preparation features remain in planning. The unavailable list separately names Windows Autopatch, Feature updates, Quality updates, Expedite updates, and Driver updates for GCC High and DoD. Government administrators should distinguish the available user-driven path from planned functionality.

keyChanges.title: Multi Admin Approval Graph API guidance is retired from Learn
keyChanges.detail: The dedicated “Use Multi Admin Approval with the Microsoft Graph API” article was removed. Its former guidance described opt-in access policies, interception of app-authenticated calls that modify protected Intune resources, HTTP 403 responses when required approval headers were missing, and no impact on read-only GET operations. This is a documentation retirement; the diff does not establish that MAA or app-auth enforcement was retired.

2026-06-08.headline: Configuration Manager 2603 adds internet access for Entra token validation
2026-06-08.overview: The week was mostly documentation maintenance, but several changes have direct administrative consequences. Configuration Manager 2603 introduces a management-point internet prerequisite for Microsoft Entra token validation, while Intune begins gradually rolling out Multiple Managed Accounts and changes the configuration path for the Managed Home Screen exit password. Configuration Manager also adds SQL Server 2025 support, and its integrated Connected Cache is slated for future deprecation. A Cloud PKI page now lists a lower CA maximum, but the supplied evidence does not establish that the service-side quota changed.
2026-06-08.adminImpact: For Configuration Manager 2603, validate management-point outbound connectivity in the system context and allow the required Entra endpoints; environments using only on-premises Active Directory authentication are unaffected. For Android Enterprise COBO and COSU devices, move Managed Home Screen exit-password configuration from app configuration policies to device configuration profiles. Verify tenant availability and the supported Teams version before planning Multiple Managed Accounts assignments. Begin evaluating standalone Microsoft Connected Cache, while treating the Cloud PKI three-CA wording as a planning signal to verify against the live service because it is supported here only by a documentation diff.

keyChanges.title: ConfigMgr 2603 introduces a management point network prerequisite
keyChanges.detail: Starting in version 2603, Microsoft Identity Service Essentials validates Entra tokens and the management point requires internet access when the site supports Entra-joined users and devices and clients authenticate with Entra tokens, typically through a cloud management gateway. The guidance names https://login.microsoftonline.com and https://sts.windows.net; if a proxy is used, it must be configured at the system level.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen moves exit-password configuration to device profiles
keyChanges.detail: For Android Enterprise corporate-owned fully managed and dedicated devices, the Managed Home Screen exit lock task mode password can no longer be configured through an app configuration policy. Admins must create or update a device configuration profile to set or rotate the password.

keyChanges.title: Multiple Managed Accounts begins a gradual Teams iOS and iPadOS rollout
keyChanges.detail: The new Intune MAM capability lets users manage multiple work or school accounts in one supported app, with app protection enforced independently for each account. Current support is Microsoft Teams on iOS/iPadOS version 8.10.0 or later. One account can be MDM+MAM managed, additional accounts must be MAM-only, and multiple MDM management isn't supported.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager Connected Cache integration is headed for deprecation
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Connected Cache integration in Configuration Manager will be deprecated in a future release. After deprecation, it will receive no further feature development or updates within Configuration Manager, and Microsoft advises customers to transition to the standalone version. No retirement date is supplied.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI documentation now lists three certificate authorities per tenant
keyChanges.detail: The updated Cloud PKI index changes the documented maximum from six CAs to three for both licensed and trial tenants. It also retains the limitation that trial-created CAs use software-backed keys and cannot be converted to HSM-backed keys. This is evidence of a documentation change, not definitive proof of a service-side quota change.

2026-06-15.headline: Personally owned Android work profiles move toward web-based Android Management API enrollment
2026-06-15.overview: Android Enterprise BYOD is the week’s largest operational shift: personally owned work-profile management is moving from the Company Portal custom DPC to Android Management API, with browser-based enrollment and a documented opt-in migration path. Intune also changed Win32 content delivery to require HTTPS, made Apple ADE enrollment-time grouping generally available, and added a GCC High-only, audit-only STIG baseline. A June 2026 Message Center change moves Microsoft 365 Apps policy configuration to the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center without changing existing policies. Other sampled edits mainly clarify enrollment procedures and navigation.
2026-06-15.adminImpact: Android administrators need to plan the migration and account for the Chrome or Edge requirement and the current passkey-only authentication limitation. Organizations using Microsoft Connected Cache must configure HTTPS to keep serving managed Win32 content from cache; otherwise clients fall back to the CDN. Apple ADE administrators can use enrollment-time grouping in new policies, while GCC High administrators should treat the STIG baseline as an assessment and reporting tool rather than an enforcement profile. Update Microsoft 365 Apps runbooks to use the separate admin center; existing policies remain unchanged.

keyChanges.title: Android Enterprise personally owned work profiles transition to AMAPI
keyChanges.detail: This is a transition in enrollment and policy delivery, not an immediate universal cutover. Intune is moving personally owned work-profile management from the Company Portal custom DPC to Android Management API. Administrators can enable web-based enrollment for new devices and deploy the Move to Android Management API policy for existing devices. Web enrollment uses Chrome or Edge, and if passkeys are the only accepted authentication method, Microsoft says not to enable it until web-enrollment passkey support is 신

keyChanges.title: Managed Win32 app content now requires HTTPS delivery
keyChanges.detail: This is a changed security and content-delivery requirement. When Microsoft Connected Cache nodes aren't configured for HTTPS, clients bypass those nodes and download managed Win32 apps from the content delivery network instead. Administrators relying on Connected Cache should configure and validate HTTPS on their cache nodes.

keyChanges.title: Apple ADE enrollment-time grouping reaches general availability
keyChanges.detail: Enrollment-time grouping is now generally available for Apple automated device enrollment on iOS/iPadOS and macOS, with support in new enrollment policies. During enrollment, Intune can identify a device's Microsoft Entra security group so applicable policies, apps, and settings can be applied earlier in setup.

keyChanges.title: GCC High gains an audit-only Windows STIG baseline
keyChanges.detail: This new Intune security baseline assesses Windows devices against DISA Security Technical Implementation Guide recommendations. The initial baseline is the Microsoft Windows 11 STIG SCAP Benchmark Version 2, Release 7, dated January 5, 2026. It is read-only and generates audit reports without configuring or enforcing settings; availability is limited to GCC High tenants with Advanced Analytics licensing.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft 365 Apps policy configuration moves out of Intune
keyChanges.detail: This planned configuration-location change begins with Intune's June 2026 release: Microsoft 365 Apps policy settings will only be configurable in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center, not the Intune admin center. Existing policies and functionality remain unchanged, but administrator guidance and runbooks should point future policy configuration to the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

2026-06-22.headline: Intune’s upcoming iOS/iPadOS 18 and macOS 15 support floors demand planning
2026-06-22.overview: The period is dominated by documentation maintenance: 561 of 568 records are updates, and representative diffs largely normalize admin-center links, punctuation, and wording. The substantive exceptions are two Message Center plan-for-change notices for Apple platform support, Enterprise App Catalog auto-update guidance, a Windows 25H2 security-baseline setting, and Microsoft 365 Apps baseline version 2512. Two new Trustd Mobile articles add integration and setup guidance, but the supplied evidence does not establish a launch, preview, or general-availability announcement.
2026-06-22.adminImpact: Use Intune inventory and reports to identify iOS/iPadOS devices below version 18 and macOS devices on 14.x or below, then plan upgrades before Apple’s respective releases. Treat userless ADE devices separately because their iOS requirements differ. Review which Required Enterprise App Catalog assignments should use auto-update; Available assignments retain the existing workflow. For Windows 25H2 baseline profiles created before the June update, edit and save the profile so the new setting deploys at the next device check-in. If you use the Microsoft 365 Apps baseline, review version 2512 and its documented defaults before changing baseline plans.

keyChanges.title: Planned support change: iOS/iPadOS 18 becomes Intune’s minimum
keyChanges.detail: After Apple’s iOS/iPadOS 27 release later this year, Intune will require iOS/iPadOS 18 or higher. The notice directs organizations to use Intune compatibility checks and reports to identify affected devices; userless devices enrolled through Automated Device Enrollment have different OS-version requirements.

keyChanges.title: Planned support change: macOS 15 becomes the new enrollment floor
keyChanges.detail: After Apple’s macOS Golden Gate 27 release this year, Intune will support macOS 15 and later. Devices already enrolled on macOS 14.x or below remain enrolled, but new enrollments on those versions will no longer be allowed.

keyChanges.title: Capability guidance: Enterprise App Catalog auto-update is assignment-scoped
keyChanges.detail: Updated Enterprise App Management guidance documents automatic updates for Enterprise App Catalog apps with a Required assignment. Intune detects newer catalog versions and updates targeted devices without requiring a new app or per-update supersedence relationship. The scope is Windows 10 and Windows 11 catalog apps; apps assigned Available for enrolled devices retain the existing workflow, while Guided update supersedence remains an alternative.
keyChanges.product: Enterprise App Management — Enterprise App Catalog

keyChanges.title: Changed baseline behavior: Windows 25H2 adds IE11 COM automation blocking
keyChanges.detail: The June 2026 service update added Disable Internet Explorer 11 Launch Via COM Automation to the version 25H2 Windows security baseline with a default of Enabled. Profiles created before the update do not apply the setting automatically: administrators must edit and save them, after which Intune deploys the change at the next device check-in. New or updated version 25H2 profiles include it by default.

keyChanges.title: Security baseline update: Microsoft 365 Apps version 2512 replaces 2306
keyChanges.detail: The Intune reference now documents Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise security baseline version 2512, first made available in June 2026, replacing version 2306. Listed defaults include Block Flash activation in Office documents = Enabled, Restrict legacy JScript execution for Office = Enabled, and Allow Trusted Locations on the network = Disabled. The article directs administrators to the Security Compliance Toolkit for the full 2512 settings.
keyChanges.product: Intune — Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise security baseline

2026-06-29.headline: Security Copilot agent guidance adds an Intune RBAC permission-delay warning
2026-06-29.overview: The supplied period is dominated by documentation maintenance rather than evidenced product rollouts: many representative edits change collection metadata, author fields, or typography. Two substantive documentation changes stand out. Security Copilot guidance now calls out RBAC permission propagation for the Vulnerability Remediation Agent, while Intune’s third-party compliance partner page replaces Kandji with Iru. Neither diff, by itself, establishes a product retirement or tenant behavior change.
2026-06-29.adminImpact: Allow several minutes for Intune RBAC permissions to take effect after adding the Vulnerability Remediation Agent’s agentic user to a group before troubleshooting access. For third-party compliance integrations, review internal references to the partner list, but do not infer from this documentation diff alone that Kandji support was retired or that Iru availability changed in the service.

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability Remediation Agent guidance adds an RBAC propagation warning
keyChanges.detail: The Security Copilot Vulnerability Remediation Agent page now adds an IMPORTANT note that permissions assigned through an Intune RBAC role may take several minutes to take effect after the agentic user is added to the group. This is operational troubleshooting guidance, not evidence of a new agent capability.

keyChanges.title: Intune’s third-party compliance list replaces Kandji with Iru
keyChanges.detail: The Third Party Partners page removes the Kandji entry and its Kandji Device Compliance link, replacing them with an Iru link for Microsoft Device Compliance getting started guidance. The change establishes a documentation listing change, but does not establish a Kandji retirement or a change in tenant support.

2026-07-06.headline: Microsoft 365 E3 and E5 start receiving bundled Intune Suite capabilities
2026-07-06.overview: The consequential item is a gradual rollout of selected Intune Suite capabilities into commercial Microsoft 365 E3 and E5: eligible tenants are automatically provisioned, with a Microsoft 365 admin center notice 30 days beforehand and no action required. The other meaningful items are documentation clarifications: Configuration Manager now spells out baseline first-evaluation conditions and Graph consent for Azure service-secret renewal, while Android web-enrollment guidance retains passkey and phone-call MFA limitations. No retirements or Message Center announcements were recorded; the remaining edits are low-impact Apple naming and macOS Company Portal procedure changes.
2026-07-06.adminImpact: Commercial Microsoft 365 E3 and E5 administrators should watch for the 30-day admin center notice, but no provisioning action is required. Configuration Manager operators troubleshooting missed baseline evaluations should check the documented power and idle conditions and Scheduler.log. Secret-key renewal in Configuration Manager 2409 requires an account able to grant Microsoft Graph Directory.Read.All consent. keyChanges.detail: Microsoft says Microsoft 365 E3 receives Remote Help, Advanced Analytics, and Intune Plan 2 through the included EMS E3 entitlement. Intune Plan 2 includes Microsoft Tunnel for mobile application management, specialty device management, and firmware over-the-air updates for supported devices. Microsoft 365 E5 adds Endpoint Privilege Management, Enterprise Application Management, and Microsoft Cloud PKI. The rollout is gradual, eligible tenants are automatically provisioned, and no action is required; Education and6

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager clarifies when a baseline first evaluates
keyChanges.detail: The Deploy Configuration Baselines page now says that, after the first evaluation on a client, computer-targeted deployments are evaluated within a two-hour randomization window of each scheduled start time. The first evaluation on a Windows client also requires the device to be powered above the low-battery threshold and the user to be idle. This is a documentation clarification, not evidence of a product behavior change this week.

keyChanges.title: Azure Services Wizard guidance specifies Graph consent for 2409 renewal
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance says that, starting in Configuration Manager 2409, Azure services use Microsoft Graph. Renewing the secret key requires consent for Microsoft Graph Directory.Read.All, which the Cloud Application Administrator role can't grant. Administrators must use Global Administrator or another role that can grant admin consent for Microsoft Graph permissions. The change documents the 2409 prerequisite rather than announcing a new rollout.

keyChanges.title: Android web-enrollment guidance retains the passkey-only limitation
keyChanges.detail: The Personal work profile page removes statements that the limitation will be resolved in a future update, but still says users can't complete web enrollment when passkeys are the only accepted authentication method. It continues to advise against enabling web enrollment until passkey support is announced. The phone-call MFA caveat and the secondary-device or SMS workaround remain; no support date or behavior change is announced.

2026-07-13.headline: Configuration Manager guidance flags manual SQL collation checks before site database moves
2026-07-13.overview: Configuration Manager’s revised infrastructure guidance is the week’s highest-impact item: the Modify SQL Server configuration path doesn’t run the collation prerequisite check, so administrators must verify both the target instance and site database themselves before moving. Intune’s standout content change expands the documented custom-compliance workflow to macOS Bash discovery scripts, with a 10-minute maximum runtime and explicit format and exit-code rules. Most remaining updates are maintenance or clarification, including link corrections, support-matrix entries, and Software Center session wording. The supplied record contains no evidence of a new preview, GA release, launch, or retirement.
2026-07-13.adminImpact: Run the supplied SQL verification script against CM_<sitecode>, not master, and resolve every ERROR before using Modify SQL Server configuration; confirm that both the target SQL Server instance and site database use SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. For macOS custom compliance, use Bash scripts with a valid shebang, UTF-8 encoding without a BOM, a runtime of 10 minutes or less, and exit code 0 for success or nonzero for failure. When troubleshooting software-update scans, separate forced/cache behavior from online/WSUS and offline/local-metadata behavior. Under AllSigned, use a packaged signed .ps1 with the Package and Script name options rather than embedding the script. Treat MDM Delete status Completed as server-side completion only, not confirmation that the client finished Retire.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager move guidance adds a manual SQL collation check
keyChanges.detail: The updated Modify infrastructure article adds an IMPORTANT warning that the Modify SQL Server configuration maintenance path does not run the collation prerequisite check performed by a new install or upgrade. Both the target SQL Server instance and site database must use SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. A verification script must be run against the site database, CM_<sitecode>, rather than master, and every ERROR must be resolved before continuing. This is operational safety guidance, not a newly announced migration

keyChanges.title: Intune custom-compliance guidance now documents macOS Bash constraints
keyChanges.detail: The discovery-script article changes its documented scope from Linux and Windows to Linux, macOS, and Windows. macOS scripts use Bash, must run in 10 minutes or less, require a valid shebang such as #!/bin/bash, must be UTF-8 encoded without a BOM, and must return exit code 0 for success or a nonzero code for failure. The procedure adds an example that reads the Microsoft Intune Agent app version and directs administrators to set the logged-on credentials, signature-check, and hidden-notifications settings to Yes.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager separates software-update scan forcing from WSUS connectivity
keyChanges.detail: The revised Software Updates Introduction treats forced versus non-forced and online versus offline as independent decisions. Non-forced scans reuse current cached results within the TTL; forced scans always run a new scan. Non-forced online scans contact WSUS only when the cache is outside the TTL, forced online scans always contact WSUS, and forced offline scans use local metadata without contacting WSUS. The page also clarifies that one scan evaluates the whole synchronized catalog, not an individual deployment.

keyChanges.title: AllSigned task sequences should use packaged signed scripts
keyChanges.detail: A new Configuration Manager note warns that Enter a PowerShell script may not preserve signed content byte-for-byte through task-sequence XML. The signature can become invalid, causing the client to reject the script and smsts.log to record a “hash does not match” error. Under AllSigned, the documented workaround is to place the signed .ps1 file in a Configuration Manager package and reference it with the Package and Script name options.

keyChanges.title: Intune Delete status separates server completion from client Retire
keyChanges.detail: The revised action guidance states that Delete removes a device from Intune management and immediately hides it from the admin center; the Device actions report records the action as Completed. For MDM devices, Delete initiates Retire, but Completed means the server-side process is finished and does not confirm that the client device completed Retire.

2026-07-20.headline: Client-driven compliance preview centers on proactive Windows reevaluation as macOS guidance flags LAPS expiry
2026-07-20.overview: The week of 20 July was dominated by documentation maintenance: 2,515 of 2,517 recorded changes were updates, 2,482 were associated with Configuration Manager, and no removals or Message Center items were supplied. The meaningful Intune diffs describe client-driven compliance evaluation as a Windows preview, warn about macOS compliance password side effects, and document an Endpoint Privilege Management scope-tag limitation. A settings catalog tutorial also adds dynamic-group targeting references. Nothing in the supplied evidence establishes a general-availability launch or retirement.
2026-07-20.adminImpact: Windows compliance administrators should account for supported devices proactively requesting reevaluation after local configuration or security changes, rather than relying solely on scheduled check-ins; the capability is explicitly preview. Before changing macOS compliance password requirements, account for automatic password expiry across all device accounts, including LAPS and Platform SSO, and consider the documented settings catalog alternative with Change At Next Auth set to False. EPM RBAC designers cannot use scope tags with the two named roles and should use the documented Device configurations Read-permission workaround where applicable. The large Configuration Manager batch and BlackBerry edits are metadata or link maintenance in the supplied diffs and indicate no tenant action

keyChanges.title: Client-driven compliance evaluation is documented as a Windows preview
keyChanges.detail: Intune compliance-policy guidance adds “Client-driven compliance evaluation (preview)” for supported Windows devices. Devices can detect certain local state changes—including device configuration, security posture, and other compliance-affecting settings—and proactively request a compliance reevaluation instead of waiting for the next scheduled check-in. This is preview guidance, not evidence of general availability.

keyChanges.title: macOS password requirements carry an all-account expiry warning
keyChanges.detail: The macOS compliance settings reference now warns that requiring a password in a compliance policy automatically expires the existing password for all accounts on the device, including accounts created by LAPS and Platform SSO. It recommends managing device passwords with a settings catalog policy and configuring Change At Next Auth to False. The diff documents this side effect; it does not establish that the behavior is newly introduced.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint Privilege Management roles do not support scope tags
keyChanges.detail: The EPM known-issues guidance states that the built-in “Endpoint Privilege Manager” role and the custom “Endpoint Privilege Management Policy Authoring” role do not support scope tags. To restrict an administrator’s view permissions using scope tags, the documented workaround is to grant permissions that include Read for “Device configurations.”

keyChanges.title: Settings catalog tutorial adds dynamic-group efficiency references
keyChanges.detail: The settings catalog policy walkthrough adds links for creating simpler and faster dynamic membership rules, optimizing rule efficiency, and choosing the right targeting method in Intune. This is an ordinary documentation clarification and related-content addition; the diff does not indicate a change to dynamic-group behavior or settings catalog functionality.
keyChanges.product: Intune — Settings catalog and group targeting

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager volume is largely metadata normalization
keyChanges.detail: The supplied Configuration Manager representative diffs show mechanical metadata changes, including replacing ms.subservice “core-infra” with “core-infrastructure” and adding ms.service “microsoft-endpoint-configuration-manager.” These are documentation taxonomy edits, not evidence of a product feature, retirement, security fix, or changed administrator procedure.

2026-07-27.headline: Controlled Defender configuration preview locks devices to Intune-delivered security settings
2026-07-27.overview: The week of 27 July was update-heavy—35 items were updated, one was new, and none were removed—but several changes have direct administrator relevance. Intune introduced preview documentation for controlled Defender configuration, while service release 2607 lists Samsung Knox E-FOTA and new Windows and Edge catalog settings. The Windows Sync page specifies expanded Windows processing, and Configuration Manager guidance changes the proxy context for MISE token validation. Configuration Manager’s new SQL Server page and related cross-reference edits are primarily guidance clarification. The supplied evidence does not label any of these feature entries generally available.
2026-07-27.adminImpact: Treat Controlled Configuration as a preview and note that **Off (Default)** leaves the capability disabled; review existing Group Policy, Configuration Manager, third-party, and local-script conflicts before a scoped test. For service release 2607, verify that devices use one of the listed corporate-owned Android Enterprise modes before evaluating E-FOTA, and use the documented Settings catalog path for the new Windows controls. On Windows, the expanded Sync flow and **Device sync status** tab can support troubleshooting, but the page limits this behavior to Windows. Configuration Manager 2603 management points using a proxy require Local System WinINET settings, not site-system or WinHTTP proxy settings. Also review KB 38232642 for CVE-2026-47301 and the Message Center recommendation for

keyChanges.title: Controlled Configuration (Device) adds a Defender authority mode in preview
keyChanges.detail: The **Controlled Configuration (Device)** setting is documented under the **Windows Security experience** profile for Antivirus policy. Its values are **Not configured**, **Off (Default)**, **Tamper Protection (On)**, and **Controlled Configuration (On)**. The new mode makes Intune-delivered Defender settings take exclusive precedence over other management channels; settings not configured in Intune use secure defaults. **Tamper Protection (On)** retains the existing secure-default behavior.

keyChanges.title: Intune service release 2607 adds Samsung firmware and Windows catalog controls
keyChanges.detail: The July 27 service-release entry says Intune now integrates Samsung Knox E-FOTA for Android Enterprise corporate-owned dedicated (COSU), fully managed (COBO), and corporate-owned with work profile (COPE) devices. Admins can select firmware versions, deploy without user interaction, and schedule downloads and installations. The same entry adds Windows Settings catalog options for camera behavior, Keyboard Filter controls for Windows Insider devices, and WSL, plus Edge 149 templates (version 149.0.4022.21) with new,

keyChanges.title: Windows Sync guidance specifies multi-workload processing and status tracking
keyChanges.detail: The updated Sync page states that selecting **Sync** on Windows initiates on-demand processing across compliance evaluation, configuration policies, app detection and deployment state, scripts and remediations, and other device-management signals. Administrators can track progress in the **Device sync status** tab in the device overview. The page explicitly says this behavior and tab apply only to Windows.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2603 requires Local System WinINET for MISE proxy validation
keyChanges.detail: For version 2603, Microsoft Entra token validation on the management point runs in the **Local System** context through the .NET Framework HTTP stack. A site-system proxy or machine-wide WinHTTP proxy set with `netsh winhttp set proxy` is not used. Configure the proxy in the Local System account’s WinINET settings, including `ProxyEnable` and `ProxyServer` under `HKEY_USERS\S-1-5-18\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings`, or configure Internet Options in the system context.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager hotfix guidance now identifies CVE-2026-47301
keyChanges.detail: The KB 38232642 page now explicitly says its security update for importing console extensions resolves **CVE-2026-47301**. This is updated security guidance identifying the affected vulnerability; the supplied evidence does not provide a deployment deadline or indicate a new Intune capability.

2026-08-03.headline: MDM Firewall and ASR policies expose policy-level, not per-setting, status
2026-08-03.overview: The week’s substantive Intune update clarified Endpoint Security reporting: Firewall Rules and Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) Rules policies managed through MDM show policy-level status only, while per-setting status requires devices enrolled with Defender for Endpoint security settings management. The other update corrected procedure numbering in Monitor Device Profile. The supplied evidence indicates documentation clarification rather than a feature launch, preview, general-availability change, retirement, or product behavior change.
2026-08-03.adminImpact: Set reporting expectations for MDM-managed Firewall Rules and ASR Rules policies: policy-level status does not include per-setting statuses. If per-setting status is required, devices must be enrolled with Defender for Endpoint security settings management. The Monitor Device Profile renumbering requires no tenant action.

keyChanges.title: Firewall and ASR per-setting reporting limitation clarified
keyChanges.detail: The Firewall documentation states that per-setting reporting is available for most Endpoint Security policies, but MDM-managed Firewall Rules and ASR Rules policies are limited to policy-level status. Per-setting status for those policies requires enrollment with Defender for Endpoint security settings management.

keyChanges.title: Monitor Device Profile procedure steps were renumbered
keyChanges.detail: The reporting procedure now labels “Go back to Device and user check-in status and select View report” as step 6 instead of step 5, and the following policy-property information step as 7 instead of 6. This is a documentation procedure correction, not evidence of a functional change.

2026-01.headline: Replace “Require approved client app” before June 2026 Conditional Access retirement
2026-01.overview: January’s clearest administrator deadline is the planned June 2026 retirement of the Microsoft Entra Conditional Access “Require approved client app” control; Microsoft directs organizations to “Require application protection policy” instead. A separate March change ends Microsoft Defender for Android protection of personal profiles on enrolled devices, while corporate work profiles and unenrolled devices remain unaffected. Beyond those notices, the supplied evidence is documentation-heavy but includes Configuration Manager’s MDT retirement, sharper Windows quality-update guidance, a 25-app Windows Autopilot device-preparation limit, and new Cloud PKI deployment material. The Cloud PKI additions describe cloud CA and BYOCA deployment models, CA creation, and audit procedures; they do not establish a separate January launch or general-availability announcement.
2026-01.adminImpact: Inventory Conditional Access policies using “Require approved client app” and replace that control with “Require application protection policy” before June 2026. No remediation is required for the announced Defender for Android scope change. Configuration Manager teams should remove MDT task-sequence steps before removing MDT integration. For Windows servicing, use update rings for ordinary monthly quality updates and validate the documented prerequisites before using expedited updates or Hotpatch. Revisit Autopilot device-preparation timeouts before assigning larger app sets. Cloud PKI planners should choose between a cloud root/issuing CA hierarchy and BYOCA, and verify the required CA-creation permissions.

keyChanges.title: June retirement of the approved-client-app control
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft 365 Message Center says the Microsoft Entra Conditional Access “Require approved client app” control retires in June 2026. After retirement it will no longer be enforceable; the stated replacement is “Require application protection policy,” which provides equivalent and enhanced protection. This is a planned control retirement, not a documentation-only rename.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Android drops enrolled personal-profile protection
keyChanges.detail: By March 2026, Microsoft Defender for Android will stop protecting personal profiles on enrolled devices and focus on corporate work profiles. The notice says work profiles and unenrolled devices are unaffected and requires no administrator action. This is a change in protection scope and behavior.

keyChanges.title: MDT integration and standalone MDT are retired
keyChanges.detail: Configuration Manager release notes now state that MDT integration with Configuration Manager and MDT Standalone are no longer supported. Customers must remove all MDT task-sequence steps and then remove MDT integration to prevent task-sequence corruption and modification failures; Microsoft points to Windows Autopilot or supported operating-system deployment instead. This is a retirement with a concrete cleanup sequence.

keyChanges.title: Quality-update guidance limits expedited deployments
keyChanges.detail: New Intune guidance separates ordinary monthly quality updates, which continue to use Windows Update ring policies, from expedited deployment. Only eligible Windows security updates can currently be expedited; Windows versions earlier than 24H2 require Update Health Tools, and preview-build settings, non-default automatic-update behavior, notification suppression, and several Group Policy settings can interfere. This is operational prerequisite guidance, not evidence of a separate general-availability announcement.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot device preparation limit rises to 25 apps
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Autopilot device preparation “What’s new” page records a limit increase to up to 25 apps in a device-preparation policy, applying to user-driven and automatic modes, including all Cloud PC offerings. The page dates the change January 30, 2026 and warns administrators to adjust deployment timeouts when configuring more apps.

2026-02.headline: Intune reports will exclude devices inactive for 12+ months starting late February
2026-02.overview: February was dominated by Learn maintenance and clarification rather than evidenced feature launches. The clearest service-level change is a late-February reporting rule: devices inactive for 12+ months will be excluded from Intune reports. The most actionable documentation updates add an iOS/iPadOS Automated Device Enrollment MFA limitation, record Hybrid Entra join Autopilot timeout fixes, expand documented Endpoint Privilege Management support-approved request scope to all device users, and spell out Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management prerequisites.
2026-02.adminImpact: Rebaseline report dashboards after the change; Microsoft says no action is needed, but devices need to check in to remain in reports. For modern-authentication Automated Device Enrollment on iOS/iPadOS, provide an alternate MFA method because Setup Assistant doesn't support phishing-resistant MFA. For Hybrid Entra join Autopilot deployments, verify relevant OS builds include KB5065789 or later for 25H2, KB5065426 or later for 24H2, or KB5070312 or later for 23H2. Before using Intune security tasks for Defender vulnerabilities, verify Intune Plan 1, Defender for Endpoint, the service-to-service connection with Microsoft Intune enabled in the Defender portal, device onboarding, and risk-assessment policies. For Endpoint Privilege Management support-approved workflows, allow for requests from

keyChanges.title: Reports will omit devices inactive for 12+ months
keyChanges.detail: Message Center says that, starting late February 2026, Intune will exclude devices inactive for 12+ months from reports to improve accuracy. Reported counts may fall; Microsoft says no action is required, and devices must check in to remain in reports. This is a changed service behavior.

keyChanges.title: ADE Setup Assistant requires alternate MFA for modern authentication
keyChanges.detail: Updated Automated Device Enrollment guidance adds a caution that phishing-resistant MFA isn't supported on Setup Assistant for iOS/iPadOS. Users enrolling through Automated Device Enrollment with modern authentication need an alternate MFA method to complete enrollment. This is an enrollment limitation and security guidance update, not a launch claim.

keyChanges.title: EPM support-approved requests are not limited to primary users
keyChanges.detail: The updated Endpoint Privilege Management guidance says support-approved elevation requests can be submitted by all users of a device and aren't limited to the device's primary user. Administrators should treat this as updated operational scope for approval workflows.

keyChanges.title: Hybrid Entra join Autopilot timeouts map to specific OS fixes
keyChanges.detail: Windows Autopilot known-issues guidance now lists Hybrid Entra join deployment timeouts with error 0x80004005 and identifies fixes: KB5065789 or later for 25H2, KB5065426 or later for 24H2, and KB5070312 or later for 23H2. This is issue-resolution guidance, not a new deployment capability.

keyChanges.title: Defender Vulnerability Management prerequisites are now explicit
keyChanges.detail: The remediation article now uses Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management terminology and adds prerequisites: Intune Plan 1, Defender for Endpoint, a service-to-service connection with Microsoft Intune enabled in the Defender portal, and policies to onboard devices and enable risk assessment. This clarifies setup requirements rather than announcing a new integration.

2026-03.headline: Intune Data Warehouse reset and hotpatch defaults set administrators’ next deadlines
2026-03.overview: March’s strongest Intune signals were operational rather than a single broad release. A planned Intune Data Warehouse change threatens reporting continuity; Windows Autopatch is preparing default hotpatch behavior for eligible devices; and Windows Autopilot device preparation now supports managed-installer sequencing before app installation. Security Copilot also has a phased Microsoft 365 E5 inclusion notice, while its Vulnerability Remediation Agent is documented as a limited public preview. Much of the remaining supplied material is documentation maintenance—path corrections, title cleanup, and clarifications such as Application control remaining template-based—so it should not be read as broad product behavior change.
2026-03.adminImpact: Back up Data Warehouse data, review dashboards and queries for refreshed surrogate keys and licensing-definition changes, and move from the beta Power BI connector to the Intune admin center’s OData feed before the expected mid-June update. Identify Autopatch-eligible devices, verify prerequisites such as Virtualization-based Security, and prepare for the April opt-out setting if the May default is unsuitable. For Autopilot device-preparation deployments, review managed-installer and app ordering. For Security Copilot, track the April 20–June 30 phased E5 rollout, the allocation of 400 Security Compute Units per 1,000 users, and possible charges for advanced capabilities. Do not plan broad Vulnerability Remediation access: the supplied guidance limits it to select preview customers.

keyChanges.title: Data Warehouse update resets history and ends the beta Power BI connector
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft’s Message Center places the Intune Data Warehouse infrastructure update in mid-June 2026. It will reset historical data to about 30 days, refresh surrogate keys, and revise licensing definitions. The beta Power BI connector will be discontinued; administrators must switch to the OData feed from the Intune admin center and back up data beforehand. This is a planned change, not a completed reset.

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopatch will default eligible Intune devices to hotpatching in May
keyChanges.detail: Starting May 2026, Windows Autopatch will enable hotpatch security updates by default for eligible Intune devices. An opt-out setting will be available from April 2026, while devices still need prerequisites such as Virtualization-based Security. Hotpatching is intended to speed security updates without requiring restarts.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot device preparation adds managed-installer support before app deployment
keyChanges.detail: The updated Windows Autopilot device-preparation guidance says managed installer policy is applied during OOBE before Win32, Microsoft Store, and Enterprise App Catalog apps install. Those app types were previously skipped to avoid installation conflicts and deployment failures. This changes application sequencing for Autopilot device-preparation deployments.

keyChanges.title: Security Copilot begins phased Microsoft 365 E5 inclusion with 400 SCUs per 1,000 users
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft says Security Copilot inclusion with Microsoft 365 E5 will roll out from April 20 through June 30, 2026, providing 400 Security Compute Units per 1,000 users and core agentic features across Microsoft security products. Additional advanced capabilities may incur extra costs. This is a planned phased entitlement change, not evidence that every advanced Intune capability is included.

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability Remediation Agent remains limited to select preview customers
keyChanges.detail: New Intune guidance identifies the Vulnerability Remediation Agent as a limited public preview available only to a select group of customers. It uses Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management data to identify CVEs, prioritize remediation, and provide summarized impact analysis, suggested actions, affected systems, and step-by-step Intune remediation guidance. Administrators should not treat it as generally available; interested customers are directed to their sales team.

2026-04.headline: Edge for Business gains cross-tenant MAM as Intune’s compliance guidance expands
2026-04.overview: April’s clearest service-level change is a Message Center major update: Edge for Business now supports opt-in cross-tenant Intune MAM policies for devices managed by different tenants, including app protection, OneDrive download redirection, and leak controls. The other selected items are primarily new Learn guidance or support documentation—not proof that a new feature launched. The third-party compliance list is explicitly labeled generally available, while the EPM, WSL, and Enterprise App Catalog entries provide rollout procedures and operational clarification.
2026-04.adminImpact: Evaluate the Edge capability for opt-in contractor and partner scenarios, focusing on app protection, download redirection, and leak controls. For EPM standard-user migrations, use the documented audit settings and allow 24 hours for reporting data to appear; the guide says longer observation periods may be useful. For WSL compliance, install the Intune WSL plugin, ensure the management extension can install, and remove existing custom WSL compliance policies before setup. For partner MDM and Enterprise App Catalog deployments, confirm licensing and prerequisites, preserve Microsoft-validated app defaults unless deliberately changing them, and plan around the documented update timelines.

keyChanges.title: Edge for Business adds opt-in cross-tenant Intune MAM
keyChanges.detail: The Message Center major update says Edge for Business can apply Intune MAM policies on devices managed by a different tenant. The opt-in feature enforces app protection, redirects downloads to OneDrive, and activates leak controls. This is a product behavior update, not a documentation-only addition.
keyChanges.product: Intune MAM / Microsoft Edge for Business

keyChanges.title: Third-party compliance partner support is documented as generally available
keyChanges.detail: The new Intune overview labels its supported partner list as generally available, including Jamf Pro, Kandji, Ivanti Neurons for MDM, and Omnissa Workspace ONE UEM. It says partner-collected state is added to Microsoft Entra ID and that the partner becomes the MDM authority for devices assigned through an Entra user group. The documented sequence is to configure Intune and groups, configure the partner to send data, and then enroll devices.

keyChanges.title: EPM guidance prescribes audit-first migration from administrator to standard user
keyChanges.detail: The new Endpoint Privilege Management guide sets an audit-first path. Its example policy uses Endpoint Privilege Management: Enabled; Default elevation response: Not Configured; Send elevation data for reporting: Yes; and Reporting scope: Diagnostic data and all endpoint elevations. It says reporting data can take 24 hours to return and may warrant observation over many weeks. This is rollout guidance, not a new EPM availability announcement.

keyChanges.title: WSL compliance guidance names plugin, management-extension, and cleanup prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The new Intune WSL procedure requires the Intune WSL plugin and the Intune management extension. The extension can be installed when a PowerShell script or proactive remediation, Win32 or Microsoft Store app, or custom compliance policy is assigned. keyChanges.title: Enterprise App Catalog guidance sets validated defaults and update expectations
keyChanges.detail: The new Enterprise App Management procedure says Microsoft configures and confirms default installation, requirements, and detection settings for catalog apps, and warns that changing install or uninstall commands can introduce unexpected or harmful commands. It documents Windows Autopilot support for blocking catalog apps in the Enrollment Status Page and Device Preparation Page. Most updates are expected within 24 hours, while updates requiring manual testing typically take seven days. The page identifies EAM as7

2026-05.headline: Cloud PKI documents staged CA renewal while Intune warns against trusting device-reported values
2026-05.overview: May was heavily maintenance-oriented, with 968 updates among 1,014 entries, but several diffs have concrete administrator relevance. A new Cloud PKI article documents staged certificate-authority renewal; Intune compliance reporting adds explicit warnings about unvalidated device-reported values; custom-compliance guidance replaces Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 with 10 on one supported-platform listing; Security Copilot documents delegated permissions for the Vulnerability Remediation Agent; and Windows Autopilot guidance removes the preview label while adopting Windows 365 Flex terminology. Most items are documentation or security-guidance changes. The Autopilot edit is an availability signal, not supplied proof of general availability, and the evidence does not establish a broad retirement or tenant-wide enforcement change.
2026-05.adminImpact: Cloud PKI administrators should review renewal permissions, eligibility, staged activation, and the impact of expired CAs before certificate issuance is at risk. Update compliance-reporting runbooks so Setting values are treated as untrusted context rather than enforcement evidence. Revalidate custom-compliance rollout assumptions for RHEL 8 and RHEL 10, audit the Vulnerability Remediation Agent’s delegated Intune and Defender permissions, and update internal Windows 365 references from Frontline to Flex while confirming current Autopilot availability before rollout. The single Message Center item provides no feature-level detail that warrants additional action.

keyChanges.detail: A new Cloud PKI article describes renewal for Intune-managed and bring-your-own-CA issuing CAs. Renewal always creates a new public/private key pair, preserves access to certificates and CRLs from earlier CA versions, and can be performed through the Intune admin center or Microsoft Graph.
