The documented permissions are Read CAs andว

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability Remediation Agent guidance defines delegated run permissions
keyChanges.detail: The updated Security Copilot guidance says the agentic user needs delegated permissions assigned outside the Intune admin center, in Microsoft Entra and Microsoft Defender. In Intune, the documented option is Read Only Operator or a custom role with Mobile apps/read and Device configurations/read; the Defender requirement is a granular custom RBAC role equivalent to Unified RBAC Security Reader. The same Intune permissions are listed for viewing results.

keyChanges.title: Compliance reports now warn that Setting values are unvalidated device output
keyChanges.detail: A new compliance-reporting section describes a Setting value column that can show information reported directly by a device, application, or administrator-supplied script. Intune does not validate or enforce the content, which may include free-form text, URLs, or file paths. The guidance says to use these values only for context, not as the sole basis for administrative action, and to independently verify links or files before opening them.

keyChanges.title: Custom-compliance guidance replaces RHEL 8 with RHEL 10 in its platform list
keyChanges.detail: The custom-compliance documentation changes the listed Red Hat Enterprise Linux version from 8 to 10. It also reiterates that administrators must prepare a JSON file and discovery script, upload the script before creating the compliance policy, and select that script when configuring the policy. This is a documentation scope and procedure change; the supplied diff alone does not prove that a service-side support retirement occurred.

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopilot automatic mode guidance drops its preview label
keyChanges.detail: The Windows 365 automatic-mode article removes “preview” from its title, description, headings, and public-preview note. It also replaces Windows 365 Frontline with Windows 365 Flex for shared and dedicated scenarios and related links. The change signals updated availability and terminology guidance, but the supplied evidence does not establish general availability.

2026-06.headline: Apple’s iOS 18 and macOS 15 support floors top Intune’s June changes
2026-06.overview: June was mostly documentation maintenance: 680 of 698 records were updates, and many sampled diffs only normalized admin-center links, punctuation, or wording. The substantive exceptions were future Apple support-floor changes, a Microsoft 365 Apps policy-configuration move, newly documented Enterprise App Catalog auto-update scope, and a new read-only STIG assessment path. The Microsoft 365 Apps baseline page also says version 2512 replaces version 2306; the supplied evidence does not label these documentation additions as preview or general-availability launches.
2026-06.adminImpact: Use Intune inventory and reports to identify iOS/iPadOS devices that may fall below version 18 and macOS devices on 14.x or below; plan upgrades around Apple’s later-2026 releases, treating userless ADE devices separately. Update Microsoft 365 Apps runbooks to use the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center without recreating existing policies. Review Required Enterprise App Catalog assignments if auto-update is appropriate; Available assignments retain their existing workflow. DoD organizations can use the STIG baseline for assessment and reporting, but should not expect it to configure or enforce settings. Review Microsoft 365 Apps baseline version 2512 and its documented defaults before changing baseline plans.

keyChanges.title: iOS/iPadOS support requirement will rise to version 18
keyChanges.detail: This Message Center plan for change says Intune will require iOS/iPadOS 18 or later after Apple’s iOS/iPadOS 27 release later this year. Userless devices enrolled through ADE have different OS requirements, so device compatibility and Intune reports need separate review. This is a future support-floor notice, not an immediate retirement announcement.

keyChanges.title: macOS support will move to version 15 and later
keyChanges.detail: After Apple’s macOS Golden Gate 27 release later this year, Intune will support macOS 15 and later. Existing devices on macOS 14.x or below remain enrolled, but new enrollments on those versions will not be allowed. The notice supplies no exact enforcement date.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft 365 Apps policy settings move out of Intune
keyChanges.detail: Starting with Intune’s June 2026 release, Microsoft 365 Apps policy settings will be configurable only in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center, not the Intune admin center. Existing policies and functionality remain unchanged, making this a change to the administration path rather than policy behavior.

keyChanges.title: Enterprise App Catalog guidance defines Required-only auto-update scope
keyChanges.detail: The updated Enterprise App Management article says Enterprise App Catalog apps can automatically update when auto-update is enabled and the app has a Required assignment. The scope is Windows 10 and Windows 11; apps assigned Available for enrolled devices retain the existing update workflow, and guided update supersedence remains an alternative. This is an added documentation description, not an explicit preview or general-availability announcement.

keyChanges.title: New STIG baseline guidance is explicitly audit-only
keyChanges.detail: New Intune guidance documents a read-only Security Technical Implementation Guide audit baseline for Windows 10 and Windows 11. The listed Microsoft Windows 11 STIG SCAP Benchmark is version 2, Release 7, with 197 rules and a January 5, 2026 benchmark date. Intune assesses current configuration and provides per-setting and per-device reports through the admin center, Graph API, or CSV, with XCCDF compliance reporting; unlike other security baselines, it does not configure or enforce settings.

2026-07.headline: Commercial E3 and E5 tenants begin receiving bundled Intune Suite capabilities automatically
2026-07.overview: Most July records are maintenance edits, but the supplied diffs identify several administrator-relevant exceptions. The largest is a gradual commercial Microsoft 365 E3 and E5 entitlement rollout: eligible tenants are automatically provisioned and receive a 30-day Microsoft 365 admin center notification. Intune also documents two previews—client-driven compliance reevaluation and controlled Defender configuration—while macOS compliance content gains a Bash workflow and an account-password warning. The evidence does not establish a general-availability release or retirement; the macOS entries are documentation and security guidance rather than proof of changed service behavior. The period’s sole Message Center item separately recommends Windows KB5101684 Preview for IT1431577.
2026-07.adminImpact: Commercial Microsoft 365 E3 and E5 administrators do not need to provision the newly bundled capabilities; monitor the advance notification and gradual rollout. Treat both Intune previews as preview features and validate their effects in controlled scopes. For macOS compliance, check script format and runtime requirements, and assess password-expiry consequences before enabling password requirements. Follow normal Windows update validation procedures for the KB5101684 Preview recommendation.

keyChanges.detail: Microsoft is gradually adding Remote Help, Advanced Analytics, and Intune Plan 2—including Microsoft Tunnel for mobile application management, specialty device management, and firmware over-the-air updates for supported devices—to Microsoft 365 E3. Microsoft 365 E5 includes those capabilities plus Endpoint Privilege Management, Enterprise Application Management, and Microsoft Cloud PKI. keyChanges.title: Client-driven compliance reevaluation is documented as a Windows preview
keyChanges.detail: Supported Windows devices can detect certain local state changes—including device configuration and security-posture changes—and proactively request a compliance reevaluation instead of waiting for the next scheduled check-in. Administrators should account for this alternate evaluation timing when interpreting compliance results; the supplied evidence labels the capability preview and does not establish general availability.

keyChanges.title: Custom compliance guidance adds macOS Bash scripts and strict execution requirements
keyChanges.detail: The custom compliance discovery-script procedure now documents macOS alongside Linux and Windows. macOS scripts use Bash, must run in 10 minutes or less, include a valid shebang, be UTF-8 encoded without a BOM, and return exit code 0 for success or a non-zero code for failure. This is a documentation expansion; the supplied diff does not establish a new service rollout.

keyChanges.title: macOS compliance guidance warns that password requirements expire every device account
keyChanges.detail: The macOS compliance reference now warns that requiring a password in a compliance policy automatically expires the existing password for all accounts on the device, including accounts created by LAPS and Platform SSO. It recommends managing device passwords through a settings catalog policy with Change At Next Auth configured to False. This is security guidance and a behavior clarification, not evidence that the service behavior newly changed.

2026-08.headline: MDM Firewall and ASR reporting stays policy-level without Defender enrollment
2026-08.overview: August’s two Intune updates were documentation clarifications rather than a feature launch. The Firewall page now states that MDM-managed Firewall Rules and Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) Rules policies provide policy-level status only, while per-setting status requires devices enrolled with Defender for Endpoint security settings management. Monitor Device Profile received corrected procedure numbering.
2026-08.adminImpact: Set expectations that MDM-managed Firewall Rules and ASR Rules policies do not provide per-setting reporting. If per-setting status is needed, the affected devices must be enrolled with Defender for Endpoint security settings management. The Monitor Device Profile numbering correction requires no tenant configuration change.

keyChanges.title: Firewall and ASR MDM policies have limited reporting
keyChanges.detail: The Firewall documentation clarifies that, although per-setting reporting is available for most Endpoint Security policies, Firewall Rules and ASR Rules policies managed through MDM report policy-level status only. Per-setting status requires devices enrolled with Defender for Endpoint security settings management.

keyChanges.title: Monitor Device Profile procedure steps were renumbered
keyChanges.detail: The procedure now identifies “Go back to Device and user check-in status and select View report” as step 6 instead of step 5, and the subsequent policy-property review as step 7 instead of step 6. This is a documentation correction, not evidence of changed product behavior.
